summary: The incident is a failure of the external exchange partner api.exchange-partner.example (vendor-owned, no telemetry), not a defect in order-service v2.15.2. Every hop of the causal chain below the shared origin is verified: order-service's 504s are 100% "exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)" (F8); exchange-gateway's own upstream_error_rate steps 0.3% -> 45-46% locating the fault below it (F10); logs pin the failing endpoint to the single host api.exchange-partner.example with 5000ms connect timeouts plus genuine L7 503s carrying x-partner-request-id (F11/F31/F32/F33); and the shared-edge scope is confirmed by market-data-service and api-gateway stepping in the same bucket while pricing-engine on a separate path stays flat (F19/F21/F24). Confidence is high (0.80). The reporter's prime suspect, dep-5333, is contradicted by mechanism mismatch and by the absence of any recovery in the ~1h37m after its rollback (F8/F14).

ranked_hypotheses.title: External exchange partner (api.exchange-partner.example) outage — dependency_failure, matching HIST-103
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external exchange API api.exchange-partner.example (vendor-owned, has_telemetry=false, F30) began failing/timing out around 10:54Z. exchange-gateway's calls to that single host block on the 5s connect timeout and also receive genuine L7 503 responses, so exchange-gateway returns 504s to every consumer on the exchange-gateway->exchange-api edge. order-service's placeOrder call therefore fails ~30%, and market-data-service and api-gateway step at the same boundary, while the only service on a disparate path (pricing-engine) stays flat. order-service (and its v2.15.2 release) is only the loudest victim. The only unverified link remains the ORIGIN of the timeout (partner-side vs internal edge), which H2 and H3 share; evidence favoring partner-side: HIST-103's recorded partner-side attribution (F25/F26), zero recorded changes on the failing edge across ~6.5 months (F27/F28), and F11's real L7 503s from the partner host (a pure DNS/connect break would not yield partner-branded 503s with x-partner-request-id).
ranked_hypotheses.root_cause_service: exchange-api (api.exchange-partner.example) — external exchange partner, owned by 'vendor'

causal_chain.claim: External exchange partner degrades around 10:54Z (unreachable/slow); no recorded internal change exists on this edge and the partner has no telemetry, so by elimination and by precedent the event is external

Genuine L7 responses from the partner host (503 Service Unavailable with x-partner-request-id=) show the partner itself is answering and rejecting, not merely an unroutable name — this argues against a pure DNS/connect break on our side
exchange-gateway's own upstream_error_rate (failures of its downstream) steps ~0.3% -> 45-46%, locating the fault below exchange-gateway rather than in its serving path

Every error signature in exchange-gateway logs names exactly one host, api.exchange-partner.example (connect timeouts op=placeOrder 163 / op=quoteSnapshot 146, plus 503s 161), recurring every 20-60s for the whole window; no other host appears
The blocking 5000ms timeout drives exchange-gateway latency_p99 from ~130ms to ~5000ms and error_rate to 43-45%; circuit breaker opens 11:03:26Z at failure ratio 0.47

Every consumer of the shared exchange-gateway->exchange-api edge degrades in lockstep: market-data-service (0.24%->5.68%, F19) and api-gateway (0.23%->5.42%, F21) step at the same ~11:00Z boundary, and only this edge is common to all stepping services while pricing-engine (disparate path) stays flat
order-service's placeOrder calls exchange-gateway, blocks on the 5s timeout and returns 504; order-service latency_p99 mirrors the step to ~5300ms
order-service error_rate steps from ~0.2% to ~30% at 11:01Z and holds — a step, not a ramp; first ERROR log line 11:02:45Z

Identical signature to HIST-103 ('Order failures during exchange partner outage'), whose recorded root cause was an external exchange API outage on the partner side and whose resolution was failing over to a secondary exchange route

assumptions: api.exchange-partner.example is a true external dependency rather than an internal service with an internal fault (F30: no telemetry, appears only as a host in exchange-gateway logs)
The partner degradation began ~10:54Z independently of any internal change; F16/F27/F28 only show nothing was RECORDED on that edge, not that nothing changed out-of-band
The 5000ms connect timeout is pre-existing configuration (no recorded change, F27), not newly tightened
The 43-45% exchange-gateway magnitude is the maximum of the observed set; other consumers' lower magnitudes reflect different request mixes and circuit-breaker shedding rather than a separate cause

market-data-service's identical error step with flat p99 (F20) reflects circuit-breaker fail-fast on its cached/derived path rather than a blocking 5s call — inferred by timing, not confirmed by a matching failure signature

ranked_hypotheses.title: Internal network/DNS/egress degradation or out-of-band timeout/endpoint setting on the exchange-gateway -> partner edge
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The exchange-gateway -> api.exchange-partner.example edge fails not because the partner itself degraded but because an internal network/DNS/egress path to the partner broke, or an endpoint/timeout setting was tightened out-of-band, producing the same 5000ms connect timeouts. Category is infrastructure_failure (or config_change if a setting was changed); the fix differs from waiting on the partner. It is not eliminated: no internal-edge change is RECORDED (F27/F28 only cover the change logs), and the properties that distinguish it from H2 — a shared egress path failing across multiple hosts, or a DNS/connect-pool error signature — were never directly tested (F34: INFO host= enumeration and WARN timeout/DNS queries both returned 503; the only enumeration of hosts comes from ERROR/WARN data). Counter-evidence: F11/F31 show genuine L7 503 Service Unavailable responses from the partner host with x-partner-request-id, and the errors name exactly one host, which a pure DNS/egress break would not produce and which a shared-egress failure would likely widen beyond one host.

causal_chain.claim: Internal connectivity/DNS/egress to api.exchange-partner.example degrades (or an unlogged timeout/DNS setting changed) around 10:54Z

exchange-gateway logs 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example' for placeOrder (163) and quoteSnapshot (146) from 11:01:25Z, and 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' (161) from 11:02:20Z
upstream_error_rate steps to 45-46%; circuit breaker opens at 11:03:26Z
Because the break is on the shared exchange-gateway->exchange-api edge, all consumers step together: market-data-service (F19), api-gateway (F21) and order-service -> ~30% submit failure (F7)

assumptions: An internal DNS/egress change could be unlogged or out-of-band — F27/F28 only query the change logs, so absence there is not proof of no change

If this were an internal network fault restricted to the partner edge, the rest of the estate's egress would remain healthy — untested, as no second external edge was sampled (and the INFO host= enumeration that would list normal-path egress targets never succeeded, F34)

ranked_hypotheses.title: Shared datastore/queue (ledger-db or redis-cache/kafka) concurrency step causing order-service failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A shared platform component in order-service's graph — ledger-db (shared by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service) or the shared redis-cache/kafka — degraded at the incident onset, and order-service's 30% failures are a downstream symptom of that shared-element failure rather than of the exchange path.

causal_chain.claim: A shared component (ledger-db, redis-cache or kafka) steps at ~10:54-11:01Z — e.g. connection or replica pressure on the shared ledger-db, or a redis-cache failure shared with pricing-engine/market-data-service
order-service's submit path blocks/fails on that shared dependency
order-service error_rate steps ~0.2% -> ~30%
Other consumers of the same shared component and of order-service degrade — market-data-service, api-gateway

assumptions: A shared datastore/queue step occurred at ~10:54-11:01Z (untestable: F23 shows ledger-db and kafka expose no error_rate metric)
market-data-service and api-gateway's degradation is caused by the shared store rather than by the exchange edge they both also sit behind

ranked_hypotheses.title: order-service v2.15.2 regression (reporter's suspicion)
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The order-service v2.15.2 release (dep-5333, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit', deployed 10:48Z) introduced a defect in the submit path that causes ~30% of order submits to 5xx.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5333 deployed to order-service at 10:48Z, 13 min before the 11:01Z step
New idempotency-key / retry-safe submit code path is invoked on placeOrder
Defective code causes order submit failures
order-service error_rate steps ~0.2% -> ~21-31% and holds

assumptions: The new release code actually touches or can fail the exchange-gateway call path
No other cause explains the timing
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Mechanism mismatch (F8): 100% of errors are 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' — a dependency timeout, not an idempotency/DB code defect. F14: rollback at 11:16Z produced no recovery (error rate held ~30-31% through 12:52Z). F10/F11: the failure originates below exchange-gateway at the external exchange-api edge, a component dep-5333 does not touch (F16). Decisively, F19/F21/F24 show market-data-service and api-gateway stepping at the same boundary even though they never received dep-5333, and F22 shows the release cannot explain pricing-engine's flatness — the scope contradicts a local order-service defect.

ranked_hypotheses.title: pricing-engine cache TTL change (cfg-2290) as upstream trigger
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only config change in the window, pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 at 09:20Z (cfg-2290), perturbed the shared quote path and indirectly stressed the exchange path, contributing to order-service failures.

causal_chain.claim: cfg-2290 changes quote cache TTL 5->4 at 09:20Z
Shorter TTL increases upstream quote/exchange call volume
Added load / behaviour change degrades exchange-path calls
order-service submit 504s rise

assumptions: A 1-second TTL reduction on a quote cache could affect exchange-partner call volume
Some mechanism exists from TTL to exchange-api 503s
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: F15: the change is a 1s quote-cache TTL, not a timeout/retry/endpoint setting, and pricing-engine is only a direct callee of order-service — not on the failing exchange-gateway -> exchange-api edge. F16: no change exists for the failing component. F22 is decisive: pricing-engine's error_rate (0.17-0.23%) and latency_p99 (~59-62ms) stay FLAT across the entire 07:00-12:45Z window, so the service whose config changed shows no degradation at all, and F24 confirms it sits on a separate path from the stepping services. Timing also weakly fits (1h41m quiet gap before onset).

facts.statement: order-service error_rate steps abruptly from ~0.2% (flat 07:00-10:58Z) to ~21% at 11:01-11:04Z and holds ~30-31% through 12:52Z; first ERROR log line at 11:02:45Z.
349 of 350 matched order-service error log lines are the single pattern 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'; 100% of the errors are 504s.

exchange-gateway error_rate steps from ~0.2% (through 10:45Z) to 9.86% at 10:54Z and 43-45% from 11:03Z, with latency_p99_ms jumping from ~128-131ms to 4625.9ms at 11:00Z and ~5000-5200ms thereafter — at or slightly before order-service's 11:01Z step.
exchange-gateway's upstream_error_rate (failures of its downstream dependency) steps from ~0.3% to 45-46% from 11:03Z, locating the origin below exchange-gateway rather than in its own serving path.

exchange-gateway error logs name the failing endpoint as host=api.exchange-partner.example with 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms' for placeOrder (163) and quoteSnapshot (146), plus 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' (161); a circuit breaker opened at 11:03:26Z (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s).

Only one host appears in exchange-gateway error logs across 10:00-12:59Z: api.exchange-partner.example. Both the ERROR-level query (470 matches) and an independent '.example' WARN/ERROR query returned only that single host, and the same host recurs every 20-60s from 11:01:25Z to 12:58:32Z.

market-data-service, the other known consumer of exchange-gateway, shows the same step at the incident onset: error_rate flat ~0.18-0.24% through 10:45Z, then 5.68% in the 11:00-11:15Z bucket holding 6.49-6.63% through 12:45Z — a step, not a ramp.
api-gateway (upstream caller of order-service) shows the same step at the same time at lower magnitude: ~0.18-0.24% through 10:45Z, 5.42% at 11:00Z, ~6.1-6.2% through 12:45Z.

pricing-engine — a direct callee of order-service and the service whose cache TTL config changed at 09:20Z — shows no step on either metric across 07:00-12:45Z (error_rate 0.17-0.23%, latency_p99 ~58.9-61.6ms), i.e. the changed service itself is healthy.
Only one deployment occurred across ALL services in the 24h before onset: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit') at 2026-03-17T10:48Z, rolled_back at 11:16Z.

No deployment or config change exists for exchange-gateway in the 24h window (both count 0), and none is recorded for the failing external host api.exchange-partner.example — no recorded change touches the actually failing edge (exchange-gateway -> external exchange-api).
No config change of any kind is recorded for exchange-gateway across 2025-09-01 -> 2026-03-17T12:59Z, and no deployment of exchange-gateway is recorded across the same ~6.5-month window.
The only config change across all services in the window is pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (cfg-2290) at 09:20Z — a quote-cache TTL, not a timeout/retry/endpoint setting.

Precedent HIST-103 (2025-10-21) has the identical signature (504 on order submit, upstream timeouts) and is recorded with root_cause 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', category dependency_failure, resolved by 'Failed over to secondary exchange route; partner fixed'; no source in the available data attributes it to an internal network/DNS/egress or timeout-config change.

The external dependency exchange-api is owned by 'vendor' with has_telemetry=false, so its health can only be inferred indirectly; the dependency inventory shows exchange-gateway has exactly one external edge and no secondary/failover external exchange node in the graph.

ledger-db and kafka do not expose an error_rate metric (ledger-db: connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min; kafka: cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions), so shared-store concurrency at 10:54-11:01Z could not be assessed with the requested metric.

The INFO-level host= enumeration query in exchange-gateway failed with retryable HTTP 503 four times, and the WARN timeout/DNS query also failed with 503, so the normal-path egress host list and any DNS/connect-pool error signature could not be inspected.

assumptions: api.exchange-partner.example is a true external dependency rather than an internal service with an internal fault (F30: owner 'vendor', has_telemetry=false, appears only as a host in exchange-gateway logs). No service of that name was queried.
The partner degradation began at ~10:54Z independently of any internal change; F16/F27/F28 show only that nothing was RECORDED on that edge over ~6.5 months, not that nothing changed out-of-band.
The 5000ms connect timeout is pre-existing configuration (no recorded change per F27), not newly tightened.

The origin of the 5000ms connect timeout (partner-side vs an internal egress/DNS/timeout-config fault) is not directly verifiable: the discriminator queries failed (F34) and the partner has no telemetry (F30). The partner-side reading is favored by HIST-103's recorded attribution, the absence of any recorded edge change, and the presence of partner-branded L7 503s.

The 43-45% exchange-gateway magnitude is the maximum of the observed set; lower magnitudes at other consumers reflect different request mixes and circuit-breaker shedding rather than a separate cause.

market-data-service's identical error step with flat p99 (F20) reflects circuit-breaker fail-fast on its cached/derived path rather than a blocking 5s call — inferred by timing, not confirmed by a matching failure signature.
Metric buckets are coarse (900s for most queried services, 180s for order-service), so component onset ordering within 10:54-11:03Z cannot be resolved to the minute.
No exhaustive enumeration of exchange-gateway's callers was run; the 'all consumers degraded' scope rests on the depth-3 order-service graph plus market-data-service and api-gateway.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The services that step at ~11:00Z (exchange-gateway, order-service, market-data-service, api-gateway) are all connected to the exchange-gateway -> exchange-api path, while pricing-engine, on a separate path not calling exchange-gateway, stays flat — consistent with a shared edge below exchange-gateway.

(demoted from facts: no verified observation backs it) The rollback of dep-5333 at 11:16Z does not coincide with any recovery: order-service error_rate held ~30-31% through 12:52Z, ~1h37m after rollback.

timeline.event: Only config change across all services: pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (cfg-2290).
Only deployment in the window across all services: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333, 'Add idempotency keys to order submit').
exchange-gateway error_rate steps to 9.86% (from ~0.2%); order-service latency_p99 jumps to 726ms avg / 5326ms max. First observed degradation point.
market-data-service (0.24% -> 5.68%), api-gateway (0.23% -> 5.42%) and exchange-gateway (latency_p99 4625.9ms) step in the same 11:00Z bucket; pricing-engine remains flat.
First exchange-gateway error log: 'upstream connect timeout after 5000ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder'. Failure pinned to a single external host.
First timeout on op=quoteSnapshot against the same host.
First 'exchange-api returned 503 Service Unavailable' from the partner host (genuine L7 partner responses).
First ERROR log line in order-service: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)'.
Circuit breaker opens for exchange-api in exchange-gateway (failure ratio 0.47 over 60s).
exchange-gateway error_rate and upstream_error_rate plateau at 43-45% and 45-46% respectively; order-service error_rate holds ~30-31%.
order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333) rolled back — no recovery follows.
order-service error_rate still ~30-31%, ~1h37m after the rollback.
Last recorded exchange-gateway error log for host=api.exchange-partner.example; incident still active at latest data (12:59Z).

recommended_actions.action: Engage the vendor for api.exchange-partner.example now: report 5000ms connect timeouts plus 503 Service Unavailable responses carrying x-partner-request-id, beginning ~10:54Z, and request partner-side status/RCA.
recommended_actions.rationale: The failure originates below exchange-gateway at the single external host named in every error log (F10, F11, F31/F32/F33), and the identical-signature precedent HIST-103 was attributed to a partner-side outage and resolved by the partner fixing it (F17, F25, F26).

recommended_actions.action: Execute the HIST-103 playbook — fail over exchange-gateway traffic to a secondary exchange route if one can be configured/obtained. Note the dependency inventory shows no second external exchange node today (F29), so this requires the vendor or the exchange-gateway owner to supply an alternate endpoint.
recommended_actions.rationale: HIST-103's recorded resolution was 'Failed over to secondary exchange route' against an identical 504-on-order-submit signature (F26), but no secondary route exists in the current graph, so this must be arranged rather than assumed.

recommended_actions.action: Preserve the exchange-gateway circuit breaker setting as-is (OPEN for exchange-api, failure ratio 0.47 over 60s) and keep the v2.15.2 rollback in place; do not chase further order-service rollbacks or code reverts.
recommended_actions.rationale: The rollback at 11:16Z produced no recovery over the following ~1h37m (F14), and the error mechanism is a dependency timeout unrelated to the release (F8, F16); the circuit breaker is the only mitigation currently shedding load.

recommended_actions.action: Confirm recovery by watching exchange-gateway upstream_error_rate return toward ~0.3% and order-service error_rate return toward ~0.2%; declare resolved only when both hold for at least two consecutive metric buckets.
recommended_actions.rationale: These are the two metrics with verified step changes and their pre-incident baselines (F9, F10, F7).

recommended_actions.action: Close out the order-service dep-5333 investigation explicitly as a non-cause and re-verify the idempotency-key change independently (e.g. in staging) before any redeploy.
recommended_actions.rationale: The deployment is contradicted by mechanism mismatch (F8), by other services stepping without receiving it (F19, F21, F24), and by the absence of post-rollback recovery (F14).

recommended_actions.action: Add telemetry or a synthetic prober for the external exchange partner (api.exchange-partner.example): availability, connect-timeout rate, and 503 rate, with alerting on the 5s connect timeout boundary.
recommended_actions.rationale: This dependency has has_telemetry=false, so its health can only be inferred indirectly and the partner-side vs internal-edge distinction could not be settled from data (F30, F34).

recommended_actions.action: Institute and test a secondary/failover exchange route with an exercised runbook, so the HIST-103 resolution is executable rather than improvised.
recommended_actions.rationale: The historical resolution mechanism exists in the precedent (F26) but is absent from the current dependency graph (F29).

recommended_actions.action: Add per-consumer circuit breakers / bulkheads with fail-fast semantics on the exchange path, and make the connect timeout configurable and monitored for exchange-gateway.
recommended_actions.rationale: Consumers blocked on the 5000ms connect timeout amplify a single partner outage to 30-45% error rates across order-service, market-data-service and api-gateway (F12, F9, F19, F21, F20).

data_gaps: No telemetry exists for api.exchange-partner.example (has_telemetry=false, F30), so the partner-side vs internal egress/DNS origin of the 5000ms timeout cannot be confirmed from our data.

The final discriminator — the INFO-level host= enumeration in exchange-gateway (4x HTTP 503) and the WARN timeout/DNS query (503) — failed permanently, so the normal-path egress host set and any DNS/connection-pool error signature were never inspected (F34).

Change history was only queried for the available window; 'no change on the exchange-gateway edge' means 'nothing recorded' over ~6.5 months (F27/F28), not positive proof that no out-of-band DNS/egress change occurred.
search_historical_incidents returns only summary fields, so any later re-attribution of HIST-103 would not be visible; only the recorded partner-side attribution is confirmed (F25).

ledger-db and kafka expose no error_rate metric (F23), so a concurrent shared-store/queue step at 10:54-11:01Z cannot be confirmed or excluded; redis-cache and kafka dependency enumerations also failed or were not run.

Metric buckets are coarse (900s typical, 180s for order-service), so the exact onset ordering among order-service, exchange-gateway, market-data-service and api-gateway within 10:54-11:03Z cannot be resolved.
No error-log query was run for market-data-service or api-gateway, so the mechanism linking their error step to the exchange edge is inferred from timing rather than matching failure signatures.

Blast radius beyond order-service, exchange-gateway, market-data-service and api-gateway was not sampled, and exchange-gateway's callers were not exhaustively enumerated beyond the depth-3 order-service graph.
Log queries were truncated (order-service 40 of 350; exchange-gateway 30 of 473), so rarer error signatures may be missed.
what_would_change_the_conclusion: Partner-side telemetry or vendor confirmation showing api.exchange-partner.example was healthy at 10:54-12:59Z, which would move the origin to the internal egress/DNS/timeout-config edge (H3).

Evidence of a concurrent failure on a second, unrelated external egress target from the same order-service/exchange-gateway network path — that would indicate a shared internal egress/DNS fault rather than a single-partner outage.
A DNS-resolution or connect-pool error signature in exchange-gateway (rather than genuine partner L7 503 responses with x-partner-request-id) would favor an internal connectivity break.
Discovery of an unlogged/out-of-band change to exchange-gateway's timeout, endpoint or egress configuration around 10:54Z would revive H3 (and a config_change reading).

Recovery of order-service and exchange-gateway metrics at the same moment the partner recovers, or immediately upon a route failover, would confirm H2; conversely, continued failure at the same rate after partner-side recovery would refute it.

Evidence that only order-service degrades (e.g. market-data-service's and api-gateway's steps turn out to be unrelated to the exchange edge) would shrink the blast radius back toward a local order-service or shared-store cause.

findings.statement: Across ALL services, only one deployment occurred in the 24h before the incident: order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333), deployed 2026-03-17T10:48Z by a.khan, summary 'Add idempotency keys to order submit', status 'rolled_back' with rolled_back_at 2026-03-17T11:16Z.
One config change across all services: pricing-engine key cache.ttl_seconds changed 5->4 at 2026-03-17T09:20Z by config-bot ('Shorter quote cache TTL'), cfg-2290.

order-service's dependencies (depth 3): direct callees ledger-db (db), pricing-engine (http), exchange-gateway (http), kafka (queue-produce); pricing-engine calls market-data-service and redis-cache; market-data-service calls redis-cache and exchange-gateway; exchange-gateway calls external exchange-api; api-gateway calls order-service.
Shared components (marked shared:true) in order-service's graph: ledger-db (postgres), redis-cache (redis), kafka (kafka), all owned by platform.
ledger-db is shared by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service — so a change/issue in any of those neighbours can reach order-service via the shared ledger-db.

pricing-engine — the service whose config changed — is a DIRECT callee of order-service (order-service -> pricing-engine http) and shares redis-cache with market-data-service; pricing-engine also calls market-data-service and redis-cache.

order-service error_rate (HTTP 5xx %) is flat ~0.2% from 07:00Z through 10:58Z then steps abruptly to ~21% in the 11:01-11:04Z bucket and holds ~30-31% through 12:52Z: the rise is a step change, not a ramp. First ERROR log line in order-service is at 11:02:45Z.

The dominant order-service error signature is a single pattern accounting for 349 of 350 matched log lines: 'exchange-gateway call failed: 504 Gateway Timeout (placeOrder)' — i.e. order-service's dependency on exchange-gateway for the placeOrder operation is the failing call. 100% of the errors are 504s; the only non-error line in the window is an unrelated GC WARN at 07:03:32Z.

The only deployment across ALL services in the 24h window before the 11:01Z onset is order-service v2.15.2 (dep-5333), deployed 2026-03-17T10:48Z by a.khan ('Add idempotency keys to order submit'), changes 'Idempotency-Key header persisted in orders table' / 'retry-safe submit handler', status 'rolled_back' at 2026-03-17T11:16Z. This is the reported service's release, 13 minutes before onset — the incident report's prime suspect, but it does not touch the exchange-gateway call path.

The rollback of dep-5333 at 11:16Z does NOT coincide with any recovery: order-service error_rate was already ~21-30% at 11:01-11:04Z and held ~30-31% through 12:52Z, i.e. the symptom persisted for ~1h37m after the release was rolled back. This weakens the deployment as the root cause.

The only config change across ALL services in the window is pricing-engine key cache.ttl_seconds 5->4 (cfg-2290) at 2026-03-17T09:20Z by config-bot, description 'Shorter quote cache TTL' — 1h41m before the 11:01Z onset. pricing-engine is a DIRECT callee of order-service (order-service -> pricing-engine http) but the change is a quote-cache TTL, not a timeout/retry/endpoint setting.

No deployment OR config change exists for exchange-gateway in the 24h window (both queries returned count 0), and no change was recorded for the failing external host api.exchange-partner.example. So no recorded change touches the component/edge that is actually failing (exchange-gateway -> external exchange-api).

Precedent HIST-103 (2025-10-21, 'Order failures during exchange partner outage', services order-service + exchange-gateway) has the IDENTICAL signature — symptoms '504 on order submit', 'upstream timeouts' — and its actual root cause was 'External exchange API outage on the partner side', category dependency_failure, resolved by failing over to a secondary exchange route. Here too the reported service (order-service) was not the faulty component.

findings.statement: market-data-service (the other known consumer of exchange-gateway) shows the SAME step change at the incident onset as exchange-gateway/order-service: error_rate is flat ~0.18-0.24% from 07:00Z through 10:45Z, then steps to 5.68% in the 11:00-11:15Z bucket and holds 6.49-6.63% through 12:45Z. This is a step, not a ramp, and no pre-onset drift is visible in the 06:00-11:00Z window (us:0.24 max 0.31 at 10:45Z).

market-data-service latency_p99_ms stays FLAT across the onset: ~39.6-41.1ms avg throughout 07:00-12:59Z (10:45Z=39.99ms, 11:00Z=40.05ms, 11:15Z=40.06ms, 12:45Z=39.61ms), with no step to the ~5000ms seen on exchange-gateway. So market-data-service shares the error step but NOT the latency/timeout signature — its degradation is not a 5s blocking-on-upstream pattern.

api-gateway (upstream caller of order-service) shows the SAME step change at the same time, but at a much lower magnitude than exchange-gateway: error_rate flat ~0.18-0.24% through 10:45Z then steps to 5.42% at 11:00Z and holds ~6.1-6.2% through 12:45Z.

pricing-engine — a DIRECT callee of order-service and the service whose cache TTL config changed at 09:20Z — shows NO step at 10:54-11:03Z on either metric: error_rate flat 0.17-0.23% across the whole 07:00-12:45Z window (10:45Z=0.21%, 11:00Z=0.21%, 12:45Z=0.20%), and latency_p99_ms flat ~58.9-61.6ms (10:45Z=60.58ms, 11:00Z=61.62ms). pricing-engine remains healthy through the incident.

ledger-db and kafka do not expose error_rate (ledger-db available_metrics are connections_active, cpu_pct, disk_used_pct, replication_lag_ms, slow_queries_per_min; kafka's are cpu_pct, messages_in_per_s, under_replicated_partitions), so the concurrency on those dependencies could NOT be assessed as requested.

The set of services that step at ~11:00Z is market-data-service (0.24% -> 5.68%), api-gateway (0.23% -> 5.42%) and, per earlier team findings, exchange-gateway (0.24% -> 43-45%) and order-service (0.2% -> ~30%); all four are connected to the exchange-gateway -> exchange-api path (order-service -> exchange-gateway, market-data-service -> exchange-gateway, exchange-gateway -> exchange-api, api-gateway -> order-service), whereas pricing-engine (on a separate path, not calling exchange-gateway) stays flat. This is consistent with a shared edge below exchange-gateway rather than something local to order-service's own path, but I cannot attribute magnitudes precisely since only one consumer's full metric pair could be obtained.

There is no record anywhere of HIST-103 ever being attributed to an internal network/DNS/egress or timeout-config change on the exchange-gateway->partner edge; all historical queries returned the same partner-side attribution.

findings.statement: No config change of any kind is recorded for exchange-gateway across the entire window 2025-09-01 -> 2026-03-17T12:59Z (count 0), so exchange-gateway's connect-timeout (5000ms), retry, or any endpoint/DNS/egress setting has NO recorded change, deprecation, or expiry event. The only config change in the whole window, across all services, remains cfg-2290 (pricing-engine cache.ttl_seconds 5->4).

No deployment of exchange-gateway is recorded across 2025-09-01 -> 2026-03-17T12:59Z (count 0). The only deployment in the whole window is dep-5333 (order-service v2.15.2, 2026-03-17T10:48Z, rolled_back 11:16Z). So there is no code/binary change on the edge that could have altered timeout/DNS/egress behaviour.

The dependency inventory shows exchange-gateway has exactly ONE external edge: exchange-gateway -> exchange-api (kind 'external', owner 'vendor', has_telemetry false). No secondary/failover external exchange node or alternate route is present in the graph (nodes list contains only exchange-api as external), which bears directly on H2's stated resolution mechanism ('failed over to secondary route') and on the fix — the graph does not evidence a second configured route.

The failing external dependency exchange-api is owned by 'vendor' and has_telemetry false — i.e. it is outside our instrumented estate, and its health can only be inferred indirectly. This means the partner-side vs internal-edge distinction cannot be settled from endpoint telemetry; it rests on the recorded attribution of HIST-103 (partner-side) plus the absence of any internal change on the edge.

Every error signature in exchange-gateway logs over 2026-03-17T10:00-12:59Z names exactly one host: api.exchange-partner.example. The ERROR-level query returned total_matched 470 (first 11:01:25Z, last 12:58:32Z) with top_patterns containing only 'upstream connect timeout after <n>ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=placeOrder' (163), 'exchange-api returned <n> Service Unavailable (x-partner-request-id=<n>)' (161) and 'upstream connect timeout after <n>ms host=api.exchange-partner.example op=quoteSnapshot' (146); no other host= value appears.

3 of my 5 attempted enumeration queries failed with retryable HTTP 503 'backend unavailable (503) (gave up after 3 attempts)': the INFO-level host= query (tc-040/tc-043/tc-046/tc-047) and the WARN/connect-timeout query (tc-042/tc-045). Because the INFO-level query never succeeded, the list of normal-path host=/endpoint values is incomplete, so the absence of a second vendor host is established only from ERROR/WARN data, not from a complete INFO-path enumeration.
